title: scheduled standby activation workflows and safe rollback for multi-AZ DR drills
author: Marisol Vega
description: Motivation: Customers running Redwood Private have asked for a predictable, safe way to automate scheduled DR drills and staged AZ failovers without a human in the loop for the activation step. This PR introduces a reusable 'standby activation' workflow as runbook-as-code (Terraform + Ansible + Helm hooks) that can be scheduled from the private control plane, executed in dry-run mode, and fully rolled back if any pre-check fails. Summary of changes: 1) Terraform: new module terraform/modules/standby_activation that wires IAM, subnet tagging, and a scheduled controller resource; provides inputs for target AZs, window, and safety thresholds. 2) Installer controller: cmd/dr-scheduler - a small controller that reads scheduled activation CRs (CRD: StandbyActivationRequest) and orchestration secrets; supports dry-run, staging (pre-check -> promote -> post-check), and automatic rollback on failure. 3) Ansible: ansible/drills/activate-standby.yml and ansible/drills/rollback-standby.yml implement the operational steps (promote standby DB replica, remap VIPs, scale replicas, verify quorum). Playbooks are idempotent and include explicit safety gates (PVC snapshot, quorum check, consumer-lag verification). 4) Helm chart updates: helm/charts/installer/templates/hooks.yaml adds pre-upgrade and post-upgrade hooks to ensure Kubernetes objects used by the controller are created before workloads start; introduces a feature flag values.drscheduler.enabled. 5) Runbooks-as-code: docs/runbooks/scheduled_dr_drill.md is a templated runbook with sections: goals, blast radius, rollback criteria, dry-run checklist, and reporting hooks for the console. 6) Tests and CI: e2e tests under test/e2e/dr that run a fast smoke scenario in the local KinD-based CI job; unit tests for controller behavior added. Migration/upgrade notes: the Helm change is opt-in via values.drscheduler.enabled=false by default for existing installs. When enabled, the Terraform module must be applied to provision scheduler RBAC and the scheduled CRD. Rollback story: controller supports automatic rollback on failed post-checks; we added a new resource status condition Reason=PostCheckFailed and an action to enqueue the rollback playbook. Dry-run: "--dry-run" mode runs the entire sequence and emits a structured report without mutating cluster state. Security: least-privilege service account for the scheduler (new policy file in rbac/policies/dr-scheduler.yaml). How to test locally: 1) helm upgrade --install installer --set drscheduler.enabled=true ./helm/charts/installer 2) apply a StandbyActivationRequest CR with dryRun: true 3) run ansible-playbook --check to validate idempotency. Checklist: - [x] Terraform module implemented with variables and README - [x] Controller + CRD implemented and unit-tested - [x] Ansible playbooks with idempotency and safety gates - [x] Helm hooks and values flag - [x] Runbook document and examples - [x] CI e2e smoke job added Notes: this PR intentionally leaves operational scheduling UI integration for a follow-up (ENG-1484). The core automation and safe rollback primitives are all in this change so infra teams can start running rehearsals and scheduled drills.

review_comments: Akash Patel: Please add a TTL on the StandbyActivationRequest CR so abandoned requests don't linger. Also we need clearer audit event emissions for promotion/demotion.
Marisol Vega (author): Added ttlSecondsAfterFinished to the CR status and emitting audit events for each stage. See controller commit c3f5a2 and rbac update.
Lena Schmidt: The PVC snapshot step needs to be idempotent when storage class doesn't support snapshots. Suggest a fallback path that records a marker and proceeds with a reduced confidence level.
Marisol Vega (author): Implemented storage snapshot capability detection and fallback marker. Added tests that simulate snapshot-unavailable path and assert rollback triggers on critical thresholds.
Diego Morales: CI e2e was flaky for environment with limited CPU; consider adding a small artificial delay between promote and post-check to allow replicas to settle.
Marisol Vega (author): Added a configurable settleWindowSeconds with a conservative default (30s). We also updated e2e timing to reduce flakiness.
Akash Patel: LGTM after TTL + audit events are included.
Lena Schmidt: Approved after tests and docs updated.
Diego Morales: Approved. Left a minor comment about log verbosity (non-blocking).
release_notes: Scheduled standby activation workflows (Terraform module + controller + Ansible runbooks + Helm hooks). Adds opt-in drscheduler feature flag. Provides dry-run and automatic rollback behavior for multi-AZ DR drills. See docs/runbooks/scheduled_dr_drill.md for operational guidance.
notes: Follow-up work: UI scheduling integration (ENG-1484), metrics integration in Console (ENG-1501). We intentionally keep the feature gated off by default to avoid changing behavior for existing installs.
how_to_revert: Revert by rolling back the merge commit and setting helm value drscheduler.enabled=false; terraform destroy for the scheduler module is supported but must be coordinated with any in-flight activations.
testing_summary: Unit tests cover controller state transitions and TTL; e2e smoke job runs a full dry-run plus one live activation against KinD; ansible playbooks exercised in CI with --check and in a small integration job that uses an ephemeral Postgres replica cluster. Manual rehearsal was done on staging with a simulated consumer load.
